articles.title: Activision Blizzard exec leaks that Overwatch might become a TV series
articles.summary: Blizzard has released so many breathtaking cinematic videos for Overwatch that most of us have wondered when Blizzard would finally look into adapting the game. Well, an Activision Blizzard executive’s resume now hints that Blizzard did explore the possibility of an actual Overwatch TV show.
articles.body: Since 2014, Blizzard has released so many breathtaking cinematic videos for Overwatch that most of us have wondered when Blizzard would finally look into adapting the game to the big screen or as a TV show. (The comparisons to Pixar have been around since the very beginning.) Well, an Activision Blizzard executive’s resume now hints that Blizzard did explore the possibility of an actual Overwatch TV show, one that might even still be on the way — and there may be a Diablo one, too. [Media: According to the LinkedIn profile of Nick van Dyk, who just so happens to be in charge of the part of Activision Blizzard responsible for building TV shows and movies, he was personally involved in developing and selling an animated Overwatch TV show. The rest of his resume suggests he might have been just the man for the job: he previously worked at Disney, where he played a key role in helping the company acquire Pixar, and he apparently sold an anime-style Diablo show to Netflix as well. If that’s true, it confirms a long-time rumor that Netflix had one in the works — though it’s not clear if the show is still in production. van Dyk’s profile notes that the Overwatch TV series was only “sold,” not greenlit, and that the Diablo show was in “pre-production” at some point. Blizzard has not made any official announcement surrounding either project, so it’s possible neither one will get off the ground.

articles.title: Nashville airport to be renamed after Dolly Parton following unanimous board vote
articles.summary: In a tribute to the late country music icon, the busiest airport in her home state of Tennessee will be named after the singer.
articles.body:
Officials in Dolly Parton's home state of Tennessee have taken one more step to rename Nashville International Airport in honor of the Grammy winner.

The airport authority's board voted in favor of the move on Friday.

Parton's sister Stella and thousands of her fans have already given the move their blessing.

So long, Nashville International Airport. The facility will be renamed to honor music star Dolly Parton after the six-person board of the Metro Nashville Airport Authority on Friday voted unanimously in favor of the move.

"Today, the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority voted unanimously, 6-0, to begin the process of modifying the airport's name in honor of Dolly Parton," the board wrote in a statement . "While a final name has not yet been determined, we are working closely with the appropriate parties to thoughtfully determine how Dolly Parton's name and legacy will be incorporated."

It continued, "This vote represents the first step in a multifaceted process. In the coming months, we anticipate having more definitive plans to share regarding the next steps and implementation. We are grateful for the tremendous support and enthusiasm from our community and Dolly's fans around the world. We look forward to sharing additional details as plans are finalized."

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

Officials noted on Instagram , "This is an exciting and historic moment for BNA and Music City."

Entertainment Weekly has reached out to the airport.

Parton died Aug. 25 , following a cancer diagnosis that she kept secret from most .

Three days later, Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee formally announced plans to rename the transportation hub in honor of the "Here You Come Again" singer and philanthropist. He said he had already spoken to the icon's family.

"Dolly Parton's extraordinary life is forever woven into the fabric of our state," Lee said. "From her rural mountain home in East Tennessee to global stages, Dolly carried the Volunteer Spirit with her. At a place where Tennessee welcomes the world, it is fitting that Nashville International Airport would bear the name of our state's favorite daughter and greet travelers with the enduring legacy of Dolly's music, generosity, faith, and kindness."

Following his announcement, more than 175,000 people signed on to a Change.org campaign in support of the same objective.

The "Jolene" singer's sister Stella told CBS Mornings anchor Gayle King this week that she is in favor of that idea — and then some.

"I think it's a great idea," Stella said, before laughing. "I like it and anything they want.... I think we ought to name it United States of Dolly Parton since, you know, somebody else is naming everything something else. Why not? The state of Dolly Parton. Let's change the name of the state."

Parton was native of the state, as she recounted in songs such as "My Tennessee Mountain Home" and "Tennessee Homesick Blues."

Since Parton's death, Tennessee state Sen. Jessie Seal also proposed legislation to officially mark Sept. 25 as "9 to 5" Day in honor of her 1980 song and movie.

articles.title: Gilsons são salvos por bagunça boa de Daniela Mercury e Olodum em show no Rock in Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Trio herdou boa parte do público que deixou o show de Pedro Sampaio, mas não soube aproveitá-lo.
articles.summary: Trio herdou boa parte do público que deixou o show de Pedro Sampaio, mas não soube aproveitá-lo.
articles.body:
Os versos calminhos e apaixonados de “Love Love” (2019) serviram como um balde de água geladíssima para o bom público que saía do Palco Mundo em direção ao show dos Gilsons no Sunset, no início desta sexta-feira (12). As apresentações tiveram apenas dez minutos de diferença.

HORÁRIOS ROCK IN RIO: Confira a programação completa

O mar de pessoas, ainda com seus leques coloridos em mãos e instigadíssimo depois de galopar num cavalinho e montar num jetski do show de Pedro Sampaio , chegou em peso para conferir a apresentação, mas logo dispersou.

Sabiam poucas letras autorais da banda e aproveitaram o show para comprar mais bebidas ou fazer fotos do look dia embaixo da roda-gigante que fica em frente ao palco.

A apresentação também foi prejudicada pelo som baixo para quem estava depois da primeira torre de som.

“Daqui a pouco nossos convidados chegam”, avisavam. Daí apresentaram “Pra gente acordar” e “Proposta”, numa tentativa de tirar o público da inércia. Não conseguiram.

Depois, tentaram novamente. “Vamos começar a balançar agora, hein”.

Mas, para quem achou que tudo estava perdido, calma, havia salvação.

O Olodum subiu ao palco do Sunset após pouco menos de quinze minutos do início do show, e com um aviso: “A gente vai começar agora uma bagunça boa”.

Gilsons se apresentam com Daniela Mercury no Rock in Rio 2026 — Foto: Anderson Bordê/Agnews

Com seus tambores coloridos e um samba-reggae ancestral e inconfundível, engataram “Nossa Gente (Avisa lá)” com “Deusa do amor”. Mais na frente mostraram “Faraó”, recebendo um grande coro de volta nos refrões: “Êêêê faraó”.

O Olodum está no centro da história dos Gilsons. Não por acaso, “Várias Queixas”, maior sucesso da banda, veio justamente do repertório do bloco. Esta, claro, foi apresentada na sua versão “peace and love” dos Gilsons, não podendo ficar de fora de nenhum de seus shows. A versão do trio, lançada em 2019, foi a que mais ajudou a projetá-los nacionalmente.

Pouco depois, não sobrou para ninguém, foi a vez de Daniela Mercury dar o nome. Sua entrada foi a mais comemorada pelo público e o grande momento do show. Entrou caminhando, vestia um vestido rendado branco e usava seus cabelos cacheados soltos.

Gilsons se apresentam com Olodum no Rock in Rio 2026 — Foto: Anderson Bordê/Agnews

Bastou os primeiros versos estridentes de “Nobre Vagabundo” para o público vir junto: “Quanto tempo tem para matar essa saudade. Meu bem, o ciúme é pura vaidade”.

Ela entrou e não saiu mais. Dominou aquele espaço durante todo o tempo em que esteve no palco. “Viva o axé, viva a música brasileira, viva a democracia, a gente vai sair dessa”, repetiu.

A baiana cantou ainda um dos seus maiores hits, “Swing da Cor”, ao lado do Olodum e fez os integrantes dos Gilsons rebolarem a sua volta: “Vocês me prometeram, meninos”.

Esta foi a terceira participação dos Gilsons no Rock in Rio. Daniela também chegou à terceira edição, depois de 2001 e 2024. Para o Olodum, foi a segunda passagem pelo festival, após o encontro com o BaianaSystem em 2024.

Em um show que começou morno, José, Francisco e João Gil conseguiram entregar bons momentos: quando não estavam sós no palco.

Olodum se apresenta com Gilsons no Rock in Rio 2026 Anderson Bordê/Agnews — Foto: Anderson Bordê/Agnews

articles.title: Criolo, Amaro e Dino unem jazz, rap e MPB em show empolgante no Sunset do Rock in Rio 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Trio fez a abertura do Palco Sunset neste sábado (12).
articles.summary: Trio fez a abertura do Palco Sunset neste sábado (12).
articles.body:
Criolo, Amaro Freitas e Dino D'Santiago subiram ao Palco Sunset neste sábado (12) para unir jazz, rap, MPB e ritmos afro-lusófonos em uma celebração das conexões entre Brasil, África e Portugal.

HORÁRIOS ROCK IN RIO: Confira a programação completa

A parceria entre o rapper brasileiro, o pianista pernambucano e o cantor luso-cabo-verdiano teve início com "Esperança", canção indicada ao Grammy Latino de 2024. Definida pelos próprios artistas como um manifesto em defesa do reconhecimento, da igualdade e da transformação social, a colaboração se expandiu e deu origem ao álbum "Criolo, Amaro Freitas e Dino".

Eles abriram a apresentação com "Esperança", canção cujos versos refletem sobre o culto ao consumo, ao status e à superficialidade da sociedade contemporânea. Depois, emendaram "Você Não Me Quis" e "Menina do Coco de Carité", com direito até a uma dancinha do trio no palco.

O público se empolgou quando Criolo soltou versos de "Sebastiana", clássico de Jackson do Pandeiro.

A combinação entre piano, percussão e vozes permitiu que o show transitasse com fluidez entre momentos contemplativos e passagens de maior intensidade, abrindo espaço também para a interação.

Dino d'Santiago, Amaro Freitas e Criolo se apresentam no Rock in Rio 2026 — Foto: Anderson Bordê/AgNews

Ao longo de toda a apresentação, Dino, Criolo e Amaro demonstraram sintonia no palco, conduzindo o show com naturalidade e entrosamento.

Reflexões sociais, ambientais e identitárias atravessaram a apresentação, especialmente em faixas como "Amazônia" e "E Se Livros Fossem Líquidos (Poeta Fora da Lei Pt. II)", reforçando o caráter político e cultural do projeto.

Mas o repertório não se limitou às reflexões de caráter coletivo. A apresentação também abriu espaço para baladas românticas, como "Ela É Foda", revelando uma dimensão mais pessoal e emocional do encontro entre os três artistas.

O momento das versões de "Pérola Negra", de Luiz Melodia, e "Oceano", de Djavan, transformou a plateia em um grande coro. Enquanto Criolo cantava "Não Existe Amor em SP", Dino pintava um quadro no palco. Um medley de "Subiusdoistiozin" e "Ain't No Sunshine" também tiveram espaço no show.

Antes de encerrar o show, o telão tinha a mensagem que o show foi uma homenagem a Milton Nascimento. "O maior de todos", dizia.

Ao reunir jazz, rap, MPB e ritmos afro-lusófonos no mesmo palco, o trio construiu uma apresentação bem amarrada, em que cada elemento encontrou espaço para se destacar sem comprometer a unidade do conjunto. O encontro confirmou a força artística do projeto e foi recebido com entusiasmo pelo público do Sunset.

articles.title: Sairé em Alter do Chão: Busca dos Mastros inicia festejos | G1
articles.standfirst: Cortejo fluvial partiu da Praia das Mangueiras em direção à Praia da Arioca neste sábado (12). Programação reuniu comunidade, integrantes da corte e visitantes na vila balneária.
articles.summary: A Busca dos Mastros reuniu devotos e turistas em um cortejo fluvial pelo Rio Tapajós, iniciando oficialmente as celebrações do Sairé 2026 em Alter do Chão.
articles.body:
Mastros em Alter do Chão — Foto: Dominique Cavaleiro/g1

O Rito Tradicional do Sairé ganhou as águas do Rio Tapajós na manhã deste sábado (12) com a realização da histórica Busca dos Mastros, em Alter do Chão, em Santarém, no oeste do Pará. O evento, que marca o início oficial dos festejos que antecedem a celebração principal e o Festival dos Botos, reuniu a Corte do Sairé, moradores, devotos e turistas.

​A programação começou às 7h no Barracão do Sairé com um café da manhã comunitário. Em seguida, os participantes embarcaram em um cortejo fluvial que partiu da Praia das Mangueiras em direção à Praia da Arioca, onde os mastros de cururu e jacitara foram retirados da mata e preparados conforme a tradição ancestral.

Corte da Festa do Sairé 2026 — Foto: Dominique Cavaleiro/g1

Para as lideranças tradicionais da vila balneária, o momento simboliza a manutenção de uma herança de resistência e fé que atravessa séculos no Baixo Tapajós. Juiz da corte do Sairé, o Cacique Maduro enfatizou a dimensão espiritual e a responsabilidade de repassar o rito aos mais jovens.

​"Este é um dos momentos mais importantes do Sairé. A Busca dos Mastros não é apenas uma festa, é a nossa identidade, a nossa raiz. É uma tradição que precisamos cuidar e ensinar todos os dias para que passe para as próximas gerações e nunca se apague", ressaltou o Cacique Maduro.

​Após a travessia e o retorno do cortejo à vila, as atividades prosseguiram com almoço comunitário, ladainhas e a apresentação do tradicional grupo Espantacão.

​Presente na abertura da programação cultural e religiosa, o prefeito de Santarém, José Maria Tapajós, destacou a estrutura montada e a importância do evento para a economia e a visibilidade internacional do município.

​"Estamos trabalhando integrados para realizar o melhor Sairé de todos os tempos. A Busca dos Mastros abre com chave de ouro essa festividade que orgulha Santarém, movimenta o nosso turismo, gera renda e mostra para o mundo a riqueza da cultura amazônica", afirmou o gestor municipal.

​A festividade segue ao longo da noite a partir das 19h30, na Praça do Sairé, com a Festa dos Mastros no Palco Ludimar Lobato, trazendo atrações musicais regionais como Lobatinho, Banda 5ª Dimensão, Izellon e Banda.

articles.title: Pedro Sampaio faz festa do pijama eletrizante e lotada e mostra que merece mais que o 1º horário no Rock in Rio  | G1
articles.standfirst: DJ carioca fez o melhor show de abertura do Palco Mundo até aqui com espetáculo ‘Abraça o Amigo e Pula’, que será trabalhado por cerca de um ano.
articles.summary: DJ carioca fez o melhor show de abertura do Palco Mundo até aqui com espetáculo ‘Abraça o Amigo e Pula’, que será trabalhado por cerca de um ano.
articles.body:
Pedro Sampaio abriu a programação de um Palco Mundo do Rock in Rio entupido de gente por todos os lados neste sábado (12) com um show que marcou o início de uma nova fase da carreira.

HORÁRIOS ROCK IN RIO: Confira a programação completa

Para quem estava nos outros dias do festival, deu para notar a diferença com outras atrações que tiveram a missão de abrir o Mundo no mesmo horário ( Luísa Sonza, por exemplo ) até pelo mar de vipões espremidos nas muretinhas de vidro dos camarotes.

Depois da estética bagunceira da era “Caos”, o DJ, cantor e produtor apresentou pela primeira vez o espetáculo “Abraça o Amigo e Pula”, construído em torno de uma ideia mais íntima e acolhedora. Isso em teoria.

A principal novidade apareceu no cenário: uma estrutura de mais de dez sofás coloridos ocupou boa parte do palco em diferentes níveis, formando uma espécie de arquibancada para o artista e seus vinte ótimos dançarinos que usavam conjuntinhos de pijamas curtos e colados. A mesa de DJ de Pedro também foi transformada num sofá.

O artista já havia explicado ao g1 que o sofá simbolizava a sensação de estar aninhado, confortável, mas também funcionava como espaço para dançar, pular, fazer brincadeirinhas bobas e gostosas. Um dos sofás fazia referência à casa onde o artista morou. Outro era inspirado em “Os Simpsons”.

Ao longo do show, ele os dançarinos brincaram de guerra de travesseiros como numa boa festa do pijama. Plumas e penas voaram por todos os lados durante a batalha.

Em cerca de 28 faixas, Pedro passeou por alguns dos principais sucessos da carreira, como “SEQUÊNCIA FEITICEIRA”, “Poc Poc”, “No Chão Novinha”, “Galopa”, “Joga Pra Lua”, “Dançarina”, “Cavalinho” e o grande hit do carnaval deste ano “JETSKI”.

Em “SEQUÊNCIA CUNT”, que conta com Isma Almeida, Vita Pereira e Clementaum na versão original, Pedro chamou os três ao palco. A música é uma das que mais acenam para a comunidade LGBT+, com versos como “uma é ativa, outra é passiva”.

A faixa foi um dos momentos altos da apresentação justamente porque parece ter sido feita para o ao vivo: ganha o barulho dos 25 mil leques amarelos com azul distribuídos por ele e o coro da plateia repetindo sem parar “Cacare’, cacare’, cacare’, cunty”.

Pedro também incluiu versões de clássicões do funk, como “Só as Cachorras” no repertório. A seleção resgatou ainda “Where Have You Been”, de Rihanna, “Firework”, de Katy Perry e “Beauty and The Beats”, de Justin Bieber. “Céu Azul”, do Charlie Brown Jr., apareceu no encerramento com os versos “vamos viver, vadiar, o que importa é nossa alegria”.

Pedro Sampaio se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2026 — Foto: Leo Franco/AgNews

O grande momento aguardado pelos fãs de k-pop foi o remix de “Hootie Frutti” do grupo KATSEYE. Ele havia dado esse spoiler em suas redes. A faixa, que ainda não se tem confirmação se será lançada oficialmente, pode funcionar como forma de apresentar mais um cartão de visitas dos planos internacionais de Pedro.

Ele também prepara um álbum de funk em colaboração com Anitta para o verão de 2027, e tem chamado o projeto de “plano do dominação mundial”.

Essa aposta agressiva vem sendo construída faz tempo. Depois de levar a “Brazilian Chaos Tour” para a Europa e a América do Norte, Pedro ampliou as parcerias com artistas estrangeiros, como “G-LATINA”, com o mexicano El Bogueto, o remix de “JETSKI” com a argentina Emilia e “TÍMIDA, SANTA Y PELIGROSA”, com Cachirula e LOOJAN.

No Rock in Rio, o carioca primeiro participou de uma ativação de marca em 2022. Depois, abriu o Palco Sunset em 2024. Em junho deste ano, se apresentou na edição portuguesa.

A escalação para abrir o Mundo neste ano acontece na mesminha edição em que Calvin Harris ocupou pela primeira vez o posto de DJ headliner do palco principal.

“Um dia eu chego lá porque sei que o diferencial de um DJ para um cantor é que um DJ coloca uma outra dinâmica no show. E eu tenho a sorte de ser os dois”.

Aos 28 anos, o carioca fez questão de dizer várias vezes ao longo do show de hoje que esta era é a primeira vez dele no Palco Mundo. Só a primeira. Para as próximas, o primeiro horário já não lhe cabe mais.

articles.title: Tempo 'confuso' no Rock in Rio: público se prepara para o frio mas passa perrengue com calor  | G1
articles.standfirst: Previsão da Climatempo aponta que uma frente fria chega à cidade do Rio neste sábado (12), mas houve abertura de sol nas primeiras horas do evento.
articles.summary: Previsão da Climatempo aponta que uma frente fria chega à cidade do Rio neste sábado (12), mas houve abertura de sol nas primeiras horas do evento.
articles.body:
Público se prepara para o frio e passa perrengue com calor — Foto: Thais Espírito Santo/g1 Rio

O público que foi ao Rock in Rio neste sábado (12) estava preparado para frio e chuva, mas encontrou um sol bem tímido logo no início do festival.

A abertura do tempo deu esperança para alguns fãs, que estavam de botas, casacos e capas de chuva.

“Em Macaé faz calor, mas não tanto como aqui, eu estou morrendo de calor. Vim preparada para o frio, trouxe capa de chuva, meia extra, sacola e aí maior solzão”, diverte-se a auxiliar administrativa Júlia Fontes, que acabou recorrendo a um leque.

A jovem aprendiz Lara Cristina preparou um look com bota de couro, lenço na cabeça e casaco de pelúcia.

“Eu sou lá de Nilópolis, eu queria vir bonita, pensei nesse short e trouxe esse casaco super quente, está super quente, estou com muito calor, mas pode chover mais tarde”, explicou.

Em tom de brincadeira, ela disse que o casaco pode acabar sendo só para a foto, caso não esfrie. “Para dar close vai dar certo”.

Público que foi ao Rock in Rio neste sábado (12) estava preparado para frio e chuva, mas encontrou um sol — Foto: Thais Espírito Santo/g1 Rio

Um trio que veio do Piauí e de Brasília disse que o calor não supera o que elas estão acostumadas, mas também não chega perto do que estavam esperando.

“Viemos com capa de chuva e tudo mas não aconteceu, mas tá ótimo, só o calor que tá matando”, comentou a dentista Emme Damasceno.

A estagiária de logística Adriele Medeiros, que é de Brasília, colocou as capas de chuva no bolso da jaqueta de couro, mas estava esperançosa de não precisar usar.

Já a psicóloga Luma Santos, de Teresina, estava confortável com o tempo.

“Aqui tá melhor que Teresina pra mim, tá quase frio, mesmo elas com calor”, brincou.

articles.title: A um mês do Dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, número de fiéis começa a aumentar no Santuário Nacional | G1
articles.standfirst: Visitantes de diferentes partes do país começam a chegar à cidade; veja a programação da Festa da Padroeira
articles.summary: Visitantes de diferentes partes do país começam a chegar à cidade; veja a programação da Festa da Padroeira
articles.body:
A um mês para o Dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida , celebrado em 12 de outubro, fiéis já começaram a chegar à cidade para a Festa da Padroeira do Brasil .

Mesmo com chuva, o movimento de peregrinos já pode ser observado pelas ruas do centro de Aparecida. A expectativa é de que a quantidade de visitantes aumente nas próximas semanas, com a proximidade da data .

A enfermeira Débora Rezende veio de Ibiá, em Minas Gerais. Ela diz que nem o mau tempo tem atrapalhado a temporada em Aparecida. "O passeio está excelente. Mesmo com a chuva, a gente está saindo, fazendo as compras, indo à Basílica", disse.

Santuário Nacional de Aparecida — Foto: Gustavo Marcelino

A rede hoteleira já sente o aumento na procura. Há reservas para os primeiros dias de outubro, incluindo o caso de pessoas que preferem antecipar a visita à cidade ou que não conseguem viajar no dia 12.

Em uma rede de hotéis da cidade, mais de dois terços dos quartos já estavam ocupados para o período da festa.

Segundo o gerente-geral da rede de hotéis, Wanderson Bernardes, a procura tende a aumentar com a proximidade da celebração.

"A partir de julho todos os finais de semanas ficam lotados. Os nossos hotéis têm uma grande procura o ano todo, mas no segundo semestre, em especial nos finais de semana, essa demanda aumenta bastante mesmo", afirma o gerente de hotel Wanderson Bernardes.

Fiéis durante missa na Basílica de Aparecida . — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

Além dos romeiros que se programam para a data, há também quem prefira visitar Aparecida fora do período de maior movimento.

Uma família de São Paulo mantém a tradição de visitar a cidade todos os anos em dias antes da Festa da Padroeira , justamente para evitar a maior concentração de turistas.

"Geralmente, a gente vem antes da festa da novena e participa em casa com a imagenzinha, o altarzinho. Desta vez, nós viemos antes, e é uma alegria vir com a família", afirma a comissária de bordo, Daniela Paulino.

Para alguns visitantes, a distância e as condições do tempo também não são obstáculos.

Um grupo que saiu de Cuiabá, no Mato Grosso, onde as temperaturas estavam próximas dos 40°C, chegou a Aparecida para enfrentar o frio e a chuva. A viagem, segundo os visitantes, é motivada pela fé.

"Nós fizemos um proposito de todo ano a gente visitar a casa da mãe. Nós sentimos muito acolhidos aqui, por todos. Neste ano, eu trouxe as minhas primas para vir aqui agradecer à Nossa Senhora. Tudo vale a pena se for para agradecer à mãe", diz a servidora pública Ana Paula de Almeida.

A programação da Festa da Padroeira no Santuário Nacional ocorre entre 3 e 12 de outubro. Neste ano, o tema é “Com Maria, em comunidade, conhecer e praticar a Palavra”.

Além do Santuário Nacional, a movimentação envolve hotéis, restaurantes, lojas de artigos religiosos, comércio e outros serviços ligados ao turismo religioso.

O arcebispo de Aparecida, Dom Mário Antônio — Foto: Thiago Leon/A12

A Novena e Festa da Padroeira começa em 3 de outubro e segue até o Dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, em 12 de outubro.

A programação inclui missas, novenas, carreata, procissão, vigília e apresentações musicais.

Em 7 de outubro, haverá uma carreata. No dia 9, está previsto o Festival da Padroeira. A Procissão Memória para a Capela São Geraldo e a Vigília Mariana ocorrem dia 11.

No dia 12, o Dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, a programação começa na madrugada e segue durante todo o dia . Entre os principais momentos estão a Missa Solene, às 9h; a Consagração Solene, às 15h, na Basílica Histórica; a Missa de Encerramento, às 18h; e a Procissão Solene, às 19h30, seguida de show pirotécnico.

articles.title: J Balvin estreia no Rock in Rio, convoca Pedro Sampaio, recebe Melody 'de surpresa', e canta hit de Mc Fioti | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor colombiano foi a segunda atração do Palco Mundo neste sábado (12), penúltimo dia de festival.
articles.summary: Cantor colombiano foi a segunda atração do Palco Mundo neste sábado (12), penúltimo dia de festival.
articles.body:
Estreante no Rock in Rio, J Balvin convocou o DJ Pedro Sampaio para subir ao Palco Mundo. Juntos, eles cantaram "Perversa", feat lançado por eles em 2024. Em seguida, Pedro disse que tinha um "presente" para Balvin e chamou Melody para apresentar "Jet ski".

HORÁRIOS ROCK IN RIO: Confira a programação completa

Pedro havia acabado de se apresentar por ali e arrebatar uma multidão dançando “Cavalinho” e outros hits. Mas deixou Melody para o show de Balvin.

Depois do show de Pedro, J Balvin tinha a importante missão de manter o clima dançante antes de entregar o espaço para Demi Lovato e Maroon 5. As estrelas ainda se apresentariam ao longo da noite que tinha o “pop mainstream” como veia.

A presença do DJ brasileiro animou bem mais a plateia, que até estava empolgada (mas muitos ainda sentados) com um set inicial voltado para diversos feats do cantor com artistas pelo mundo. "Mi gente", Willy William (faixa de abertura); "Bola, rebola", um dos vários hits que tem em parceria com Anitta; "Loco Contigo", feat com Tyga; e "Con Altura", com Rosalia, estavam lá.

A interação artística entre Balvin e Pedro não é novidade. Além de terem gravado juntos a faixa "Perversa", em 2024, Balvin convidou Pedro para seu show no The Town em 2025.

Considerado um dos maiores nomes da música latina contemporânea, Balvin colocou o reggaton no cenário mundial e incluiu influências do hip-hop, R&B e pop em seu trabalho.

Estreando seu primeiro álbum em 2010, o colombiano teve sua construção musical ouvindo rap, bachata, reggae e champeta (gênero musical urbano tradicional na costa colombiana). O primeiro reconhecimento por seu trabalho aconteceu em 2015, quando venceu o Grammy Latino de Melhor Canção Urbana com “Ay Vamos”.

A primeira vez que subiu a um palco brasileiro foi em um festival sertanejo, o Villa Mix, ainda em 2017. Depois disso, ao longo dos últimos quase dez anos, já trouxe turnê solo, em 2022 (cantando para um público modesto de pouco mais de 3 mil pessoas), fez algumas apresentações no carnaval brasileiro de 2024, e marcou presença no The Town, em 2025.

Balvin emendeu várias músicas e conseguiu manter o público animado (embora bem menos engajado do que o de Pedro Sampaio) com hits como "Amarillo", "Sola Conmigo", "Ginza", "La cancion" e "Downtown", mais uma bem sucedida parceria com Anitta. Neste momento, ele declarou amor pela cantora e agradeceu: "Obrigado por me abrir as portas para o Brasil".

Ele também agradeceu a participação do público várias vezes e, segundo Pedro contou no palco, "se preocupou com a cultura brasileira pra montar esse espetáculo pro Brasil".

Balvin ainda cantou o hit "Bum bum tam tam", do MC Fioti. No The Town 2025, Balvin convocou o brasileiro. Desta vez, deixou o trecho do MC para o público.

J Balvin se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2026 — Foto: Natalia Rampinelli/Agnews

Recentemente, o cantor encerrou sua "Ciudad Primavera Tour", conhecida por um visual floral, palco em 360 graus e um extenso setlist – cerca de 50 faixas. Ao longo dela, Balvin também convocou convidados-surpresa representando cada região em que passava.

Por aqui, nem sinal do clima de flores. Usando um moletom com as cores do Brasil e um bermuda jeans rasgada, se juntou a um balé vestido todo de jeans também, em um palco sem grandes produções, mostrando que está no período de transição de turnês e, talvez, estudando novos conceitos.

Ao final do show, deixou anuncio no telão de que retorna ao Brasil em 2027.

articles.title: Kaia Gerber’s RE/DONE Knit Cutout Top Is Barely Hanging on by a Few Ties
articles.summary: Kaia Gerber is once again fronting RE/DONE, and this time, the standout piece is a knit top that’s more open than closed. The model and RE/DONE creative dire...
articles.body:
Kaia Gerber models a daring cutout knit top named the Hurston Knit Top for RE/DONE’s ‘After Hours’ campaign, featuring three functional front ties creating open cutouts from neckline to hem.

The top, made from 100% cotton in a soft black knit with rolled edges, has a slightly relaxed silhouette, three-quarter length sleeves, and a wide crew neckline, styled by Gerber with high-waisted dark denim jeans in a moody, book-lined space.

RE/DONE marks the Hurston Knit Top as ‘coming soon’ in classic black and lighter gray colorways, with sizing from XS to L and care instructions calling for a cold hand wash or dry clean to preserve the knit’s shape, as part of a collection with a literary naming convention.

Kaia Gerber is once again fronting RE/DONE, and this time, the standout piece is a knit top that's more open than closed. The model and RE/DONE creative director stars in the brand's 'Kaia Vol. 1: After Hours' campaign. The setting is a moody, book-lined space that leans heavily into old-money, literary glamour.

Kaia Gerber's RE/DONE knit top comes with risky ties and endless cutouts

Kaia Gerber models daring cutout knit top for RE/DONE's 'After Hours' campaign. The featured piece in question is the Hurston Knit Top . RE/DONE named the garment after acclaimed author Zora Neale Hurston. Made from 100% cotton in a soft black knit, the top features three functional front ties running down the center, creating a row of open cutouts from the neckline to the hem instead of a traditional closure. Rolled edges throughout give the piece a naturally lived-in feel that fits the "after hours" theme of the collection.

The top features an easy, slightly relaxed silhouette that skims the body rather than clinging to it. Three-quarter length sleeves and a wide crew neckline complete the stylish garment. In the campaign images, Gerber wears the top loosely tied, leaving noticeable gaps down the front. She pairs the garment with high-waisted dark denim jeans, balancing covered-up and daring styles in equal measure.

Styling throughout the campaign leans heavily into a bookish, after-hours mood, with Gerber photographed in front of towering bookshelves, sunglasses tucked into the top's ties, and her hair styled in loose, tousled waves. The moody lighting and library backdrop give the images an editorial, almost cinematic quality. This distinct aesthetic fits the collection's literary naming convention.

According to the product listing, RE/DONE marks the Hurston Knit Top as 'coming soon.' The brand offers a classic black option, which RE/DONE lists as 'noir,' alongside a lighter gray colorway. Sizing runs from XS to L, with care instructions calling for a cold hand wash or dry clean to preserve the knit's shape.

The top isn't the only piece from this drop making headlines. Gerber also shared campaign shots of herself wearing an unbuttoned jacket over lace-trimmed underwear. Another featured photo highlights an all-white look with a double-breasted blazer and no pants. Across the campaign, Gerber's dual role as both face and creative director shows in just how deliberately provocative each piece feels.

articles.title: Pierce Brosnan addresses Tom Hardy’s ‘Mobland’ feud: ‘It was a storm in a teacup’
articles.summary: Amid the premiere of the second season of ‘Mobland’, speculations and reports circulated about Tom Hardy’s feud behind the scenes of the show. Address.
articles.body: Amid the premiere of the second season of ‘Mobland’, speculations and reports circulated about Tom Hardy’s feud behind the scenes of the show. Addressing the matter, beloved ‘007’ star Pierce Brosnan shed some light on what really happened behind the scenes, and how everything was blown out of proportion.Pierce Brosnan talks about Tom Hardy’s ‘Mobland’ feudThe actor recently attended the London premiere for ‘Mobland 2’ where he was asked about the feud involving ‘Peaky Blinders’ star Tom Hardy. While discussing the matter with Deadline, Brosnan commented, “Oh my God, it was a storm in a teacup, really,” the James Bond star told the Press Association. “I love the dude. I love Tom Hardy. I’m a massive fan of the man’s work. Truly.” He reassured during the interview on the red carpet that everything is going smoothly within the ‘Mobland’ team, and that the issue had been something extremely small which was blown out of proportion.He added, “We are rock solid as a company, as a family. Everyone shows up for work, and everybody’s just there on the spot. It moves very fast so it’s not like we go out and socialise and go to the pub or anything like that.”Tom Hardy talks about starring in ‘Mobland’In another interview, Hardy himself commented on how big of a thing it was for him to work with the likes of Brosnan and Helen Mirren. Calling it a “privilege” while talking to PA, the ‘Venom’ actor added, “In many aspects, of course, I look up to them. Coming up, these are actors that came before me. So to be able to work with them is a privilege, but also to be able to enjoy them, watching them spread their wings with their range now as well, and play against their type in some aspects, and really enjoy that is a beautiful thing to watch as a human being.”Helen Mirren also joined the chat and talked about the show, saying, “The relationships are amazing. Obviously, Pierce and I have an extraordinary chemistry on-screen and off-screen. We’re very, very fond of each other. We respect each other enormously.”For context, reports shared online indicated that Tom Hardy had issues with the showrunner of ‘Mobland’, Jez Butterworth. Additionally, he allegedly arrived late to the set on multiple occasions, which caused issues within the team.About ‘Mobland 2’The second season of the show follows along with the story of the North London crime lord Harrigan family as they deal with rising rivals in the market. Not only that, but their attempts to take over their broken empire once more do not seem to lead anywhere, as they also wage their own internal war. articles.summary: Singer Sonu Nigam has sold a commercial property in Mumbai’s Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) for Rs 18 crore, according to property registration documents .
articles.body: Singer Sonu Nigam has sold a commercial property in Mumbai’s Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) for Rs 18 crore, according to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix. The singer sold the 3,082 sq ft commercial space nearly three years after purchasing it for Rs 14.30 crore in November 2023.The latest Sonu Nigam property sale adds to the growing list of high-value commercial real estate transactions in Mumbai’s BKC, one of the city’s most sought-after business and financial districts.According to the property registration documents, Sonu Nigam sold the commercial space on September 4, 2026. SAA Estate LLP has been listed as the purchaser, while Sonu Nigam is mentioned as the seller in the registered transaction.The property is located on the ground floor of Trade Centre, opposite the MTNL Building in BKC, Bandra East, Mumbai. The commercial unit has a carpet area of 3,082 sq ft and was sold for a consideration of Rs 18 crore.The transaction also involved a stamp duty payment of Rs 1.08 crore. Two car parking spaces were included as part of the deal, according to the documents.Sonu Nigam earns around Rs 3.70 crore on BKC propertySonu Nigam had purchased the same commercial property for Rs 14.30 crore in November 2023. With the latest sale registered at Rs 18 crore, the singer has made a gross gain of approximately Rs 3.70 crore on the property before accounting for transaction-related costs, taxes and other expenses.Based on the recorded carpet area and the consideration value, the latest transaction works out to approximately Rs 58,404 per sq ft.Kailash Kher also sold BKC office spaceInterestingly, Sonu Nigam is not the only Bollywood or music personality to have recently sold commercial real estate in the same building. Singer Kailash Kher also sold his office space in the building on September 9, 2026, for Rs 10.50 crore.Kher had purchased the property for Rs 10.50 crore in November 2025. Unlike Sonu Nigam’s transaction, the Kailash Kher deal was reportedly executed at the same consideration value at which he had acquired the office space.Sonu Nigam bought an office in Andheri WestInterestingly, Sonu Nigam had also made another commercial real estate investment in Mumbai just a month before the BKC transaction. In August 2026, the Bollywood singer purchased a 258.33 sq ft office space in Mumbai’s Andheri West for Rs 1 crore, according to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix.The transaction was registered on August 6, 2026, with Singular Health Private Limited listed as the seller and Sonu Agamkumar Nigam, the singer’s full name, recorded as the purchaser.The office unit is located in Sundervan Complex on Lokhandwala Road, Andheri West, and has a carpet area of 258.33 sq ft. Nigam paid a total consideration of Rs 1 crore for the commercial property.In addition to the purchase price, the transaction attracted Rs 6 lakh in stamp duty and a registration fee of Rs 30,000. articles.title: Norris takes Madrid pole with 'gorgeous' lap
articles.summary: Lando Norris takes a superb pole position for McLaren at the Spanish Grand Prix, beating Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
articles.body:
Lando Norris took a superb pole position for McLaren at the Spanish Grand Prix, beating Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and Red Bull's Max Verstappen in a breathless final few seconds of qualifying.

"Oh, what a lap, gorgeous," said an ecstatic Norris after pipping world championship leader Antonelli by just 0.011 seconds. "Oh, that might be my best one."

Verstappen was 0.140secs off the pace, as all three moved ahead of Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari in Madrid.

The seven-time champion had held the top spot after the first runs in the final session.

Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc was fifth, ahead of Mercedes' George Russell and the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri.

Norris' pole came from nowhere. He had been fifth in the first session of qualifying, seventh in the second, and 0.449secs slower than Hamilton's pace-setting lap after the first runs in the final session.

"I'm shocked," the world champion said. "I'm a little bit surprised to be here. It was probably one of the best laps I've done ever in my career.

"One of those laps when everything came together. I had a good idea of what I wanted to do, it was whether it came together but my brain let me do it almost perfect. It's one of those laps when you look at the time and go: 'Oh, that was pretty good."

The session had started with predictions of a crash-fest, after drivers had been warning about the high-risk nature of the new Madring street circuit, with tricky entries to corners and walls coming back at the drivers on the exits.

Two red flags during final practice had led some teams to have private sweepstakes as to how many stoppages there would be in qualifying, but the session ran cleanly, with no incidents.

Pole looked to be a battle between Antonelli and the Ferraris, with Verstappen perhaps in the mix.

In the end, the Ferraris faded, as they so often have this year when it really matters, and Norris rose to the front with a breathtaking performance.

"The adrenaline was high on the last lap," he said. "You have to relax and let it all flow.

"It's easy to get tense around here. There's a lot of walls that come at you pretty quickly. I have been feeling pretty good, I just wasn't relaxed.

"I was pretty much perfect apart from the last corner, where I thought I was in the wall. Everything I wanted to achieve I achieved and it's one of those moments when I was in that flow state."

Hamilton, who had crashed at the final corner in practice and missed the final half of the session, did improve on his last lap, but only by 0.06secs and it was not enough to prevent him falling backwards.

He edged Leclerc by just 0.006secs as Ferrari rued yet another tantalising chance slipping through their fingers.

Norris' performance was put in perspective by Piastri, who was 0.470secs off his team-mate's pace.

Russell, meanwhile, could have done with a morale-boosting performance after he finished second to Antonelli in Monza last weekend when the Italian took a stunning win from 19th on the grid.

The Briton had looked more or less on Antonelli's pace for much of the weekend, even if he clearly lacked the Italian's fluid ability to let the car run free and flow and slide on corner exits.

And in qualifying the difference was a stark 0.314secs, making more likely the prospect of the 66-point gap in the championship between them extending still further on Sunday.

The top 10 was completed by Red Bull's Liam Lawson, Alpine's Franco Colapinto and the Racing Bulls of Arvid Lindblad, the British rookie again impressing.

Local heroes Carlos Sainz and Fernando Alonso were unable to give the Spanish fans much to cheer about as both were knocked out after the first session in 17th and 18th places.

Sainz's Williams edged out Aston Martin's Alonso by just 0.076secs but faces an investigation into impeding Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas that could result in a three-place grid drop.

10. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) +1.217

articles.body: Years ago, Johnny Depp embraced the relaxing life of the South of France a little too well. In 2001, he ended up buying an entire French village! Located near Saint-Tropez, the abandoned 19th-century space consisted of a lot of small structures and a main home area. The actor at the time had bought the space to act as a vacation area and sanctuary.In 2001, Johnny Depp invested in buying and restoring a French villageIn 2001, according to a Daily Mail report, the actor bought an abandoned French Village that is situated in a commune 17 miles from Saint-Tropez. The 19th century village had been abandoned a long time ago, and when Depp bought it, the space needed quite a lot of construction work to revive its beauty. Although the actor never disclosed how much he paid for the village, he spent around USD 10 million on its reconstruction.The estate, which spans across 37 acres of land, has a main home that is worth USD 43 million, along with a gym, a chapel, a staff home, a workshop, a restaurant and bar, and around six guest houses. Along with that, according to Gentlemen’s Journal, the property also has its own underground wine cellar made in the form of a cave! He invested in creating private dining restaurants to give visitors an exclusive experience of fine dining in the South of France, with private dining spaces that mimic the style of an actual bistro. Depp named one of the restaurants in the Townsquare area as Chez Marceline, while he built another space in front of the restaurant called Blanchisserie, which translates to laundry.Johnny Depp has been trying to sell his French estate for years nowThe actor listed the estate for sale in 2015, with the first asking price set at USD 27 million. articles.summary: La valenciana ha hablado sobre ello en ‘El verano se mueve’, de Telecinco
articles.body: Aprovechando el reciente inicio de la nueva edición de ‘Supervivientes All Stars’, Carmen Alcayde ha rememorado su paso por el espacio de supervivencia, calificando el emblemático momento del salto desde el helicóptero como uno de los más estresantes de su concurso. Durante su intervención en ‘El verano se mueve’, el programa de Telecinco que presenta Ion Aramendi por las tardes de lunes a viernes, la periodista y colaboradora se sinceró sobre el verdadero impacto físico y mental que supone enfrentarse a las alturas en el reality de Honduras. "Fue horrible. Es lo peor junto con la lluvia. Es más alto de lo que parece", comenzaba diciendo. La valenciana confesó que llegó a pedir que le bajaran la aeronave “como a la Pantoja” y que el helicóptero está "mucho más alto de lo que parece" en televisión. Para ella, el miedo y la tensión de ese salto se sitúan en el escalafón más alto de los aspectos más duros del formato, llegando a afirmar que es "lo peor del programa junto con la lluvia". Aunque en su momento (durante la edición de ‘Supervivientes 2025’) intentó tomárselo con humor e incluso pidió que el helicóptero bajase al máximo para no quedar mal ante la audiencia, la colaboradora reconoce ahora que la procesión iba por dentro y el impacto emocional fue real. Finalmente, Alcayde no dudó en aplaudir a los concursantes de esta nueva edición que han reconocido la angustia que se siente desde arriba, especialmente a Asraf Beno, el marido de Isa Pantoja. “Olé, él, para que los hombres tienen que ser los valientes y las mujeres las cobardes", ha sentenciado. Cabe recordar que Carmen Alcayde dejó un buen sabor de boca durante su etapa en los Cayos Cochinos, destacando por sus alianzas y tensiones en las nominaciones. Tras enfrentarse a varias expulsiones y un paso por la zona de destierro, fue finalmente la novena expulsada de la edición en un ajustado duelo contra José Carlos Montoya.

articles.title: Oscar-winning film producer Jeremy Thomas dies aged 77
articles.summary: Best known for The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, the British film-maker was celebrated for working with international directors throughout his decades-long career.
articles.body:
Oscar-winning producer Jeremy Thomas, whose films included The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, has died aged 77.

The British filmmaker "passed away peacefully" surrounded by family and loved ones at his home in Oxfordshire on Friday, his publicist said in a statement.

Thomas built an international reputation over a career spanning five decades, working with directors including David Cronenberg, Nagisa Oshima, Julien Temple and Nicolas Roeg and backing independent films alongside mainstream successes.

He best known work, Bernardo Bertolucci's The Last Emperor, won nine Academy Awards, including best picture, and earned Thomas an Oscar as producer in 1988.

The critically-acclaimed biographical drama about the final monarch of China's Qing dynasty starred Joan Chen, Peter O'Toole and Vivian Wu.

Thomas repeatedly collaborated with Bertolucci, also producing The Sheltering Sky, Little Buddha, Stealing Beauty and The Dreamers.

He also collaborated with several British directors at the start of their careers including Ben Wheatley, Jonathan Glazer, Stephen Frears and David Mackenzie.

Thomas's other credits include Oshima's Merry Christmas, Mr Lawrence, starring David Bowie, Cronenberg's A Dangerous Method, Roeg's Bad Timing and Eureka, Fast Food Nation, The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle, and the film adaptations of the JG Ballard books Crash and High-Rise.

After beginning as a film editor, London-based Thomas landed his first production role on the 1976 Australian film Mad Dog Morgan.

In 2006 he received the European Film Academy's award for Outstanding European Achievement in World Cinema and in 2009 was made a CBE in the New Year Honours.

Thomas's latest collaboration with Japanese director Takashi Miike, Bad Lieutenant:Tokyo, is due to premiere at the Toronto Film Festival on Monday.

articles.title: Sylvan Esso think you should splurge on good-quality yogurt
articles.summary: Sylvan Esso’s new organic-sounding record Ow ∞ is out now.
articles.body: Amelia Meath and Nick Sanborn, better known as Sylvan Esso, have been bringing their low-key electro-pop to the masses since 2014, bursting onto the scene with their self-titled debut album and the single “Hey Mami.” Over the years, they’ve put out a number of excellent records, dabbling in dustier, more fragile textures on Free Love, going dancier and glitchier on No Rules Sandy. The two are constantly pushing at the edges of their sound while retaining the core of what makes a Sylvan Esso record sound like a Sylvan Esso record. Their new album Ow ∞, released this past Friday, represents perhaps the boldest reinvention of their sound, however. It’s unabashedly nostalgic-sounding, trading the glitchy modular drums and glossy dance production of Free Love for turn-of-the-century breakbeats and distorted guitars. At times, the songs recall bands like Soul Coughing and Blur, on tracks like “Hot Slob” and “Concrete Glen.” But don’t worry, there’s still plenty of bleeps and bloops and modern vocal production techniques to keep fans of past albums happy. [Media: To celebrate the release of Ow ∞ , Sylvan Esso agreed to answer our weekly questionnaire. What is your most indispensable tool? Nick Sanborn: My laptop. I have loved a series of MacBooks dating back to when I graduated from high school and cannot imagine working without one. I am absolutely one of those millennials who despises typing or doing any important work on a touchscreen. What is one thing you wish you could change about your phone? NS: I wish it felt like it cared more about me than its creator. Amelia Meath: I wish the phone was actually a food replicator. So many problems would be solved. How many tabs do you have open right now? NS: Eight, which feels a touch low compared to my normal ADHD tab expanse. No pins besides email, though, I like a tabula rasa scene when I open a browser. What is your happy place online? NS: I still frequent a version of the old Monome forum, which is generally focused on programming and instrument design. The people there are excellent and interesting and so welcoming and nice. It’s the only place on the internet that feels more positive than detrimental to me. AM: Spellsofmagic.com. What is your favorite gadget you’ve ever owned? AM: I had a T-Mobile Sidekick that I saved up for when I was in high school. It was the coolest phone I have ever owned. I kept my journal on there :D What game do you have the fondest memories of? NS: EarthBound, which was a gorgeous, heartfelt, quirky JRPG on the Super Nintendo that came out in 94. It’s beautiful and strange and full of humanity. I still play it all the way through every few years. AM: The first Zelda I played was Skyward Sword on the Wii. We lived in a house with a whole bunch of other people, and we would all hang and play together. It was a joy and became my gateway into playing games as an adult. There have been so many others that I have fallen in love with since then — Hollow Knight, Blue Prince, Hades — but Skyward Sword was my first love. So much lore. Which tech trend do you wish would go away? AM: The encouragement of apathy. What is one thing you wish you had created? NS: I rarely wish I had made something that I already like, since I feel like me making it would have ruined it being what it is in the first place. But I have been dreaming about a really specific thing — an AM/FM radio with an analog tuner that I could control remotely with a computer or sequencer — for literal years. There are many things out there that are close but not quite this, so much so that it’s kinda maddening. I even tried to get a synth tech I work with regularly to help me prototype one, but it never came to fruition. Finally, last year, a small company in Italy started making one, and like four friends sent me the link in a week, that was how endlessly chatty I had been about wanting one. Of course I ordered one, and it’s good, but I still think it could be better lol. AM: I wish I had the well. What an incredible claim to fame. “I figured out how to store and save water from the table.” I feel like I could stop trying after that. What do you do when you need to focus? AM: I go outside and sit. Usually, I have to be writing, so I can take my notebook out. I try to leave my phone inside, but I usually forget! What do you do when you’re feeling stuck? NS: I usually find myself stuck when I want something to be good and it just isn’t yet, but I can’t let it go. In that situation, I just have to step away and do something totally different and without consequence, like pulling out an instrument I haven’t used in a while and making something unrelated as spontaneously as I can. I find removing expectations and shifting gears to be really helpful for my headspace when I can’t find a way through whatever has me in a loop. When was the last time you went somewhere without your phone? NS: About a month ago, I put my phone through both the washer and dryer, destroying it completely and giving me about a week of pure phoneless existence. It was heaven. Highly recommend. What’s the last piece of physical media you bought? AM: I just bought Sheila Heti’s Pure Colour at a bookstand in Brooklyn. It is a beautiful and incredibly surreal read. What do you think is worth splurging on? NS: Yogurt. It’s not even that much of a splurge, but I just think good yogurt is utterly transcendent. Deeply underrated delicacy. What would the tagline for your biopic be? AM & NS: “Ow ∞” What’s the last GIF or meme you used? [Image: AM: This is also the last GIF I used!!!

articles.title: Celine Dion Delivers Tearful Speech on Opening Night of Paris Residency: ‘I Had Promised Myself Not to Cry’
articles.summary: Celine Dion shed tears as she kicked off her eagerly anticipated 16-date residency tonight at Plenitude Arena on the outskirts of Paris, marking her first ma...
articles.body:
Celine Dion shed tears as she kicked off her eagerly anticipated 16-date residency tonight at Plenitude Arena on the outskirts of Paris, marking her first major series of live shows since stepping away from the spotlight in 2022.

"I had promised myself not to cry," Dion told thousands of adoring fans in the opening moments of her show. "I don't keep my promises. But I'm so happy to see you all. I missed you. I'm going to sing like you without crying."

She later added, "Thank you so very much for coming. If it's your first time in Paris, I hope you fall in love with it just like I did. Finally, it's amazing we are all together. I made a promise to come back, to be back on stage. So here I am, singing for you and singing for me, singing live! Thank you so very much for your support, your patience and if I may say so, I am everything I am because you loved me."

Dion's arrival in Paris two weeks ago has dominated headlines and sparked a frenzy on social media as well as in the streets of the French capital. The metro station near the concert venue has also been renamed Celine and has been decorated with some of her most famous lyrics. Fans from every corner of the world have been camping in front of the Royal Monceau hotel behind security barriers and have been singing her more popular songs every time she comes out. Clips of Dion engaging with fans, singing a cappella with them and making some dance moves in front of the Parisian palace have gone viral.

Not all of those hardcore fans will make it to the Paris concerts, however. Some may be turned away if they unknowingly bought fake tickets from the more than 200 fraudulent websites and social media accounts that popped up right when presale tickets went on sale in April, according to the Associated Press , which quoted Group-IB, a Singapore-based cybersecurity firm.

Her comeback isn't just being eagerly anticipated by fans — it's also being touted as a potential lifeline for France's state coffers heading into 2027. French newspaper Liberation dedicated the cover of its weekend edition to Dion's residency with a picture of the singer doing a prayerlike gesture, looking upward with a bright halo of light behind her and a headline that reads, "Celine Dion — is she going to save the 2027 budget?" Her Paris concerts could indeed generate €1 billion in economic impact for France, that's four times more than what Beyoncé's Paris concerts in June 2025 brought and roughly a fifth of what the entire Paris 2024 Olympics generated, according to French radio Europe 1.

More than 33,000 people are expected at the Plenitude Arena. As much as 60% of the set list is expected to be from her French repertoire, mainly songs penned and composed by Jean-Jacques Goldman, including "Pour que tu m'aimes encore" and "J'irai où tu iras." She's also teased that her first show will last over two hours in an informal chat with fans in front of her hotel and told them to wear comfortable shoes, as reported by France Info.

Rumors have been circulating about a potential surprise duo with Beyoncé who happens to be in the French capital with Jay-Z, who gave a concert in Paris two days ago.

An estimated nine million people signed up for advance tickets for the shows after Dion announced her concert comeback on her birthday, on March 30, during a glamorous bash (which she didn't attend but delivered a message on video) in front of the Eiffel Tower, which was illuminated in tribute, with a choreographed light show set to Dion's greatest hits.

Dion made her stage return singing Edith Piaf's "Hymne A L'Amour" by the Eiffel Tower at the 2024 Paris Olympics opening ceremony.

Dion's Paris concerts were originally scheduled for 2020 at Paris La Defense Arena as part of her Courage World Tour , but were postponed due to the pandemic and then delayed again due to her health issues. In 2022, Dion was diagnosed with Stiff Person Syndrome (SPS), a rare neurological and autoimmune disorder that causes muscular stiffness, inhibiting the ability to walk and sing. Her fans lost hope she would ever come back after seeing Dion struggle against this illness in the 2024 documentary "I Am: Celine Dion," which was directed by Irene Taylor.

articles.title: Meghan Markle Reportedly Thinks She’s ‘Best Person’ To Tell Princess Diana’s Story Because ‘She’s Suffered’ Too
articles.summary: Meghan Markle reportedly wants to play a central role in Prince Harry’s rumored documentary about his late mother, Princess Diana. The Meghan Markle Reported...
articles.body:
Meghan Markle reportedly wants to play a central role in Prince Harry’s rumored documentary about Princess Diana, with the project expected to focus on Diana ahead of the 30th anniversary of her death in 2027.

Former publicist Rob Shuter claims that Meghan is helping drive the production of the documentary and wants to narrate it herself, believing she is qualified due to her previous work in front of and behind the camera.

Meghan reportedly sees parallels between herself and Diana, feeling uniquely positioned to narrate the film because, like Diana, she has suffered from relentless media scrutiny and mental health struggles in the public eye.

Meghan Markle reportedly wants to play a central role in Prince Harry 's rumored documentary about his late mother, Princess Diana . While the project was initially presented as a deeply personal undertaking for Harry, a royal commentator now claims the Duchess of Sussex is helping drive the production and wants to narrate it herself. The reported film is expected to focus on Diana ahead of the 30th anniversary of her death in 2027. However, no production company, network, streaming platform or release date has been officially announced.

According to RadarOnline , former publicist Rob Shuter discussed Meghan's alleged involvement during an appearance on Maureen Callahan's "The Nerve" podcast.

"So, when the Daily Mail broke the story that Harry was working on a movie, a TV movie about his mother, I hit the phones right away," Shuter explained. "And immediately people said, 'It's Meghan.' And it's not Harry's movie; it's Harry and Meghan's movie. It is the two of them."

Prince Harry Reportedly Reaches Out To Princess Diana's Friends

The claims followed a report from Daily Mail royal commentator Richard Kay, who said Harry had begun contacting people who knew his mother.

Kay reportedly suggested that one of Harry's reasons for returning to the United Kingdom was to work on a television film about Diana. AOL also reported that Harry had contacted some of his mother's former friends in hopes of securing their participation.

Neither Harry nor Meghan has publicly announced the project or confirmed what roles they would hold if it moves forward.

Prince Harry and Meghan reportedly "expect to be let back in" to royal life, with a source claiming the couple has "nothing else going for them."

He is moving forward with a series of public engagements amid his dispute over being labeled a "private citizen."

Meghan and Harry may be "happy" to return to the United Kingdom, but their move has already been overshadowed by fresh royal drama.

Prince Harry reportedly objected to the King labeling him and Meghan "private citizens," as the couple would have preferred to be described as "public figures."

The Duchess Reportedly Believes She Understands Television

Shuter claimed Meghan sees herself as qualified to help shape the documentary because of her previous work in front of and behind the camera. "She fancies herself as a TV producer. She has been on television shows. Some have been hits. And so, she really does feel quite, quite, quite important within the world of television," he claimed.

Meghan's best-known acting role was Rachel Zane on the USA Network legal drama "Suits." She appeared on the series from 2011 until 2018, leaving shortly before marrying Harry. "She thinks that she knows what makes a great documentary, what makes a great show," Shuter continued.

He then criticized Meghan's Netflix work, quipping, "We know that's not the case from her own stuff on Netflix." Her lifestyle series, "With Love, Meghan," premiered on Netflix in March 2025. Although reports indicated it would not return for a third season, the program later received a 2026 Daytime Emmy nomination in the Outstanding Lifestyle Program category, according to PEOPLE .

Meghan Markle Allegedly Wants To Narrate The Film

Shuter went on to claim that Meghan doesn't just want to help produce the rumored documentary. She also reportedly wants to become the voice guiding viewers through Diana's story. "So, I know she wants to do voiceovers. I know she wants to do narration. This is the project, and her husband and herself are hiring Meghan," he said.

The commentator suggested that the couple would choose Meghan over an established British performer. "They're not going to hire Judi Dench. They're not going to hire a great grand dame of the British acting world to do this. They're not going to hire Hugh Grant or some Brit with some status. They're going to hire Meghan."

Shuter's remarks remain unconfirmed, and no official announcement has identified Meghan as the documentary's narrator. The Duchess does, however, have previous experience narrating a documentary. She provided the voice-over for Disney's 2020 nature film "Elephant," which followed an elephant family on a journey across Africa.

Meghan Reportedly Sees Parallels Between Herself And Diana

Shuter claimed Meghan believes she is uniquely positioned to narrate the film because she relates to the struggles Diana experienced in the public eye. "Meghan's going to narrate the story, and she feels as if she's the best person to tell it because, like Diana, she's suffered. That's where they're going."

Meghan has previously spoken about struggling with relentless media scrutiny and her mental health while living in Britain. She and Harry have also repeatedly drawn connections between their experiences and the press's treatment of Diana. However, neither Meghan nor Harry has said publicly that those similarities are the reason she wants to narrate a film about Diana.

The rumored project would not be the first documentary Harry has made about his mother. He and Prince William participated in the 2017 film "Diana, Our Mother: Her Life and Legacy," which marked 20 years since her death and featured memories from both brothers.

articles.title: Zendaya Ditches Her Signature Curls for Shortest Hair in Years During Night Out With Hunter Schafer and Alexa Demie
articles.summary: Zendaya said goodbye to her bixie cut.
articles.body:
Zendaya ditched her signature curls for her most dramatic hair transformation yet.

The Spider-Man: Brand New Day star debuted her super-short pixie cut during a girls' night out in New York City with her Euphoria co-stars, Hunter Schafer and Alexa Demie.

Zendaya's surprise hair transformation comes less than two weeks after she celebrated her 30th birthday.

Zendaya 's 2026 press circuit has been a whirlwind of angelic waves and edgy glam. From rocking arachnid-inspired bangs during her Spider-Man: Brand New Day press tour to sporting ethereal goddess makeup during her press tour for The Odyssey , her red-carpet glam game has reached new heights. Off the red carpet, the Dune: Part Three star is proving that she doesn't need a movie premier to turn heads.

On September 11, Zendaya debuted her shortest haircut in years during a night out in New York City with her Euphoria costars, Hunter Schafer and Alexa Demie . While reuniting with her costars at Rule of Thirds, a Japanese restaurant, the Golden Globe-winner stepped showed off her ear-grazing new pixie cut , complete with textured waves that brushed against the back of her neck, per photos shared by DeuxMoi on September 12.

For the girls' night, Zendaya opted for a fitted, long-sleeved sweater in strawberry-red and a pair of white denim pants, which she styled with black loafers. She completed the look with a taupe leather tote bag.

Zendaya's dramatic hair transformation is a noticeable departure from her signature bixie hairstyle , which she's been rocking since early 2026, shortly before tying the knot with Tom Holland . Experimenting with several hairstyles in recent months, the 30 year old has been embracing her short hair's natural, curly texture on the red carpet, while occasionally opting for voluminous extensions .

Notably, on July 13, she showed off a long pixie cut with glossy bangs and curls that extended past her earlobes. Again, on August 13—shortly after her secret second wedding to Holland—the Euphoria actress debuted a subtle "shixie" cut during a day out in London with her husband. "The shixie is a haircut that falls somewhere between a pixie and a short shag, usually hitting around the ears or grazing the nape of the neck," hairstylist Sheila Guillermo told InStyle . "It features lots of soft, choppy layers that create movement and texture instead of blunt lines. It typically has volume at the crown, piecey ends, and an effortless, lived-in look."

While it's clear that Zendaya isn't afraid to experiment when it comes to her hair, her super-short pixie cut is definitely one of her most surprising—and chic—looks yet.

Zendaya's girls' night out comes less than two weeks after she celebrated her 30th birthday.

articles.title: Henry Winkler's wife says the actor tends to exaggerate about the size of his ... fish
articles.summary: Henry Winkler's wife Stacey claims the "Happy Days" star pads his fly-fishing numbers and becomes a "7-year-old" the moment he picks up a fly rod.
articles.body: Henry Winkler has been married to his wife, Stacey, for nearly five decades, so at this point, she knows him pretty well. Including, apparently, when he's exaggerating about the size of his... fish. The "Happy Days" star and his wife joined Graham Bensinger for an interview recently, where the couple talked about their marriage, how they met and the one activity that somehow transforms Winkler from one of the nicest guys in Hollywood into a fiercely competitive rule-breaker. Fly-fishing. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS According to Stacey, her husband might also be padding the stats a little bit. "You have alleged before that he pads his numbers," Bensinger said. Winkler immediately looked offended. "Wait a minute. Really?" he asked. Stacey didn't back down. "I write down in my book exactly," Winkler protested. "I don't round off. That I do only in charity." That set his wife up perfectly. "The biggest charity is your fish size," Stacey fired back. "You are about your fish size the way other people are about… other sizes." Ouch. After 48 years of marriage, Winkler seemed stunned to learn that his own wife apparently doesn't trust his measurements. "I have just learned something I've never known," he said. "I don't pad my numbers, but my wife believes I pad my numbers. Shocking. I'm shocked. I'm hurt." Who among us hasn't exaggerated a little after a fishing trip? But the (alleged) fish inflation isn't even their biggest problem on the water. The couple used to fish together, but that arrangement apparently became unsustainable because Henry — otherwise known for being an exceptionally pleasant human being — becomes an entirely different person once there's a trout involved. He explained that they once had clearly defined territory while sharing a boat. Stacey got the water from the front of the boat back to the oars. Henry got everything behind the oars. Simple enough. Except Henry didn't particularly care for that arrangement whenever Stacey's side looked more promising. "I'm here to catch a fish," he explained. "And sometimes her water on the other side of the oar looks really fishy." So his fly would occasionally "wind up" in Stacey's section. "Not wind up," she argued. "Slap into my water." TYLER HUBBARD STAYS CALM AS WIFE PULLS FISH HOOK FROM HIS SCALP ON FAMILY CAMPING VACATION Winkler insists he's simply following the fish. Stacey says her normally reasonable husband suddenly loses all regard for rules, boundaries and marital harmony the moment he picks up a fly rod. "There was just no way because he's too crazy," she said of fishing together. "He is this reasonable man who turns into a 7-year-old." In fact, the couple said their first fly-fishing experience together generated more arguments than all their previous years of marriage combined. "She just didn't understand," Henry explained. Stacey was unimpressed. "So then what I would do would be to not catch fish to make you feel better?" she asked. "That would have been so thoughtful," he deadpanned. Eventually, the Winklers found the secret to a happy fishing marriage: Don't fish together. Now they take separate boats, separate guides and even fish different parts of the river. Problem solved! Well, mostly. Because Stacey still has one surefire way to get under her husband's skin. When she catches a big fish, she sends him a photo. "He gets irritated," she said. "I do not get irritated," Winkler insisted. He just desperately wants to know how she keeps doing it. "I really think that there is something about female pheromones that attract the fish," he joked, marveling at how quickly his wife seems to hook monsters. He even floated another possibility: "Unless on the boat she can Photoshop." Stacey, meanwhile, says fly-fishing is one of the only areas of her husband's life where the famously nice, mild-mannered actor gets genuinely reckless. "If you are fishing somewhere in your area and Henry thinks he sees some bubbles or whatever, he's going there," she said. "So, there is nothing sacred." Maybe not. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER But after 48 years together, the Winklers have clearly figured out the important stuff. Separate boats. Separate fishing territory. And never, ever trust your husband's estimate of how many inches that fish actually was. Love all things fishing and outdoors? Follow OutKick OutDoors on Instagram and TikTok!

articles.title: Pink hits back amid backlash for criticizing Macklemore's pro-Palestinian concert remarks
articles.summary: Pink doubles down on criticism of Macklemore after his "Free Palestine" chants and anti-Israel song performance at a concert, sharing an emotional statement as a Jewish mom.
articles.body: Pink is doubling down on her criticism of Macklemore following his pro-Palestinian comments during a recent concert. On Sept. 4, Macklemore opened for Ed Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, and he used his time onstage to perform his anti-Israel song, "Hind's Hall." He repeatedly chanted "Free Palestine" while a slideshow played on the screen behind him, showing footage from the war in Gaza. Several fans were upset by the performance, including an Instagram page called "Stop Antisemitism." The page shared a video criticizing Macklemore, calling the move "awful." Pink reposted the video to her own Instagram story, which started a new wave of backlash from people criticizing her for seemingly being pro-Israel. MICHAEL RAPAPORT SLAMS ‘CLOWN’ MACKLEMORE FOR ANTI-ISRAEL PERFORMANCE Initially, Pink didn't explicitly share her opinion on the matter, but on Sept. 11, she took to Instagram to explain her thoughts in an emotional statement. "I’ve been quiet in my own words for a week, which you know isn’t like me. So here they are," she began. The "So What" singer explained that she'd reposted the video that was critical of Macklemore, which "said things in words I didn’t write, and I wouldn’t have chosen all of them." She maintained that "a repost isn't a statement," then wrote, "I’d rather be disagreed with for what I actually said than hated for what anybody else wrote, so let me say it." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "I was born a Jew," she continued. "I didn’t pick it, and I’ve never hidden it. And this week a whole lot of people decided what I believe without asking me, without checking a single thing I’ve ever said or done, because a repost and the word 'Jew' were apparently enough to fill in the rest. But let me fill it in... myself." "Of course I don’t speak for Israel, or for any government. I never have. What I said in October 2023 is still exactly what I believe: Hamas is a terrorist organization. Palestinians deserve a future that honors their humanity and their aspirations. Protecting innocent life comes first, everywhere, and nobody should ever celebrate the death of a child. Anybody’s child." JERRY SEINFELD GIVES BLUNT THREE-WORD RESPONSE TO INFLUENCER ASKING FOR A 'FREE PALESTINE' She detailed the work she's done with UNICEF over the years, spending time with children "on both sides of that fence," and said, "I’m not going to litigate a complex war in an Instagram caption, and I’m not going to recite anybody’s slogan to earn back a follower." Pink went on to explain that what she was "reacting to" was Macklemore himself. She recalled him performing his song "Same Love" at the Grammys in 2014, and how she cheered on the message, but "Four months later Macklemore put on a hooked nose, a black beard and a bowl cut, performed in it, and called it a 'random costume.'" "Every Jew I know knew exactly what it was. The same love, it turned out, had a guest list, and we weren’t on it. But he apologized, and I let it go, because that’s what we do. We let it go. Then last weekend he stood in front of a stadium full of music-loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn’t about them." She added, "You don’t get to decide that for us." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "That’s what prompted my repost," she wrote. "Not 'Free Palestine,' and not anyone’s right to say it. I have never asked for another artist to be silenced and I’m not asking now. I don’t need anyone fired, and I don’t need a refund. What I need is to be able to say, as a Jewish mom, 'that scared me, and it scared people I love,' without being told our fear is just propaganda, and without being told I’m somehow cool with genocide because I noticed?" Pink wrote that she's always stood up for her beliefs, even when she is criticized for it, citing her own protest song, "Dear Mr. President," which she wrote in 2006 in response to the Iraq War. "I have stood up for other people’s people my whole career, and I know exactly what it costs," she said. "And now I’m standing up for my own people, and I thought I knew going in how lonely that would be. And it’s lonelier than that. But I’m doing it anyway." "Something has changed in this country, and I can read it in my own comments. 'From the river to the sea.' 'Zionist,' spat like it’s a slur, by people who couldn’t tell you the details of what I believe, because I hadn’t told them yet. I wasn’t asked. I was told. I don’t think most of them hate Jews. I think somebody handed them a story where the Jew who won’t apologize for existing must be the villain, and they’ve been putting words in my mouth ever since." She said that while she can take being portrayed as a villain, "I just won't take it quietly, and I'm not going to teach my kids to." That’s been our unspoken agreement for twenty-five years, and it still stands, and so do I. You don’t have to agree with one thing Israel’s government does to not want the Jewish family two rows down from you to be scared or targeted at a concert. That’s the only thing I’m asking anybody for. To the ones who are frightened this week, Jewish or Muslim or Palestinian or Israeli or just tired of all of it: I see you. And if anybody wants to really know what I think, just ask me. I’m right here. I’ve never been hard to find. And I’ll keep speaking out, in my own words." She ended her post by acknowledging the anniversary of 9/11, as well as Rosh Hashanah, saying, "Now I’m going to go make dinner for my kids, light the candles, dip some apples in honey, pour a glass of wine and be full of gratitude.
